voiceLines.text: Hi. I'm really glad you're here. This first walk is five minutes, and we'll do it sitting down.
Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat, hands resting on your thighs.
Your phone can stay in your pocket. If anything hurts, just stop. There's no wrong way to do this.
Let's begin with heel taps. Lift your heels, then set them down.
If that feels fine, lift your whole foot a little. One side, then the other. That's marching.
Let your arms swing gently, like you're walking out to the mailbox.
Nice and easy. Breathe in through your nose… and out through your mouth.
Sit tall, like a string is lifting the top of your head.
If you'd like a little more, lift your knees a bit higher. Only if it feels good.
You're doing it. This is your time.
Keep that steady rhythm. You should be able to talk, or even hum along.
In a few seconds, we'll pick up the pace, just a little.
A little quicker now. Same small steps, just a bit faster.
Still able to talk? Good. That's the right pace for you.
Ten more seconds.
And slow it down. Easy marching, nice and relaxed.
Shake out your hands if you like. Keep your feet moving gently.
One more quicker round coming up. Just thirty seconds.
Quicker again. If heel taps feel better right now, that's perfect.
Want a little more? Let your arms swing a bit bigger.
Almost there. Ten seconds.
And ease off. Slow, comfortable steps.
Notice how your legs feel right now. Maybe a little warmer.
Let's start to wind down.
Slow your feet until they rest flat on the floor.
Roll your shoulders back, slowly. Two or three times.
Take a deep breath in… and let it go.
One more breath in… and out.
That's five minutes. You showed up today, and that's the hardest part.
Your first walk took you to Central Park Zoo. When you're ready, take a look. There's a postcard waiting for you.
Sit-to-stand. It helps with getting up from any chair.
Scoot to the front of your chair. Feet flat, about hip-width apart.
If you need help, put your hands on the chair and push. That's a great way to start.
Lean forward, nose over toes… and stand up.
Now sit back down, slowly. Reach back for the chair with your hips.
Take a breath whenever you need one.
Want more? Cross your arms over your chest, and sit down on a slow count of three.
Lovely. That's your last one.
Seated knee lifts. The same move you use for every step.
Hold the sides of your seat lightly. Sit tall.
Start small. Just lift your heel, then set it down.
If that feels fine, lift your whole knee a little. Then switch sides.
Keep your back tall. No need to lean back.
Want more? Lift a little higher and swing the opposite arm.
Nice and steady. Ten more seconds.
Seated leg extensions. The move you use for climbing stairs.
Sit tall and hold the sides of your seat.
Start with a small lift. Straighten your leg just halfway.
If that's comfortable, straighten it all the way, toes to the ceiling.
Keep your leg pointing straight ahead… and lower it slowly.
Want more? Hold it up for a count of three.
If your knee complains, make the lift smaller. That still counts.
Heel and toe raises. The move you use for reaching a high shelf.
Sit tall, feet flat on the floor.
Lift your heels a little, then lower them.
Now the other way. Lift your toes, heels stay down.
Small and easy is perfect.
Want more? Stand behind your chair, hold on with both hands, and rise onto your toes.
Wall push-ups. They make pushing doors and lifting bags easier.
Stand about an arm's length from the wall. Hands flat, at shoulder height.
Start by standing a little closer. Bend your elbows just a bit.
Bring your chest toward the wall… and press back.
Keep your body straight, like a plank of wood.
Want more? Step your feet back a little.
Balance time. Stand behind your chair and hold on with both hands.
Start easy. Lift just your heel, toes stay down.
If you feel steady, lift your foot a little off the floor.
Look at one spot in front of you. It helps.
Hold… you're doing great… and set it down.
If you wobble, that's normal. Hold the chair a little tighter.
Want more? Try holding on with just one hand.
Welcome back. Let's get your feet moving.
Good to see you. This walk is all at your pace.
Ready when you are. Let's start slow and easy.
Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat, back tall.
Find the front of your seat and plant your feet. Hands can rest on your thighs.
Stand near your chair so you can hold it if you need to. Feet about hip-width apart.
Stand tall with your chair close by. Soft knees, relaxed shoulders.
Step onto your walking pad and start it at a slow, easy speed.
Start your pad nice and slow. You can change the speed anytime.
Easy steps to start. Let your arms swing naturally.
Keep it light. Heels, then toes, nice and steady.
Roll your shoulders once or twice. Stay loose.
Just warming up. No rush at all.
Quicker steps coming up in a few seconds.
Get ready to pick up the pace, just a little.
A little quicker now. March your feet, and let your arms join in.
Pick up the pace in your chair. Quick, small steps.
A little quicker now. Lift your knees a bit and swing your arms.
Pick up the pace, right where you are. Stay close to your chair.
Turn your pad up a notch, or just take quicker steps.
A little faster now, if it feels right. Hold the handle if your pad has one.
Here we go again. Quicker steps.
Brisk again. Find that same rhythm.
You should be breathing a bit harder, but still able to talk.
Nice rhythm. Keep your shoulders relaxed.
If it feels like too much, slow down a little. That still counts.
Last quicker round. You've got this.
And ease off. Easy steps, catch your breath.
Slow it down. Nice and relaxed.
Let your breathing settle. You're doing well.
Easy pace. Loosen your hands.
Another quicker round in a few seconds.
Get ready. One more round coming up.
Time to wind down. Slow your feet until they're barely moving.
Time to wind down. Slow, gentle steps, then let your feet rest.
Bring your pad down to a slow stroll.
When you're ready, stop your pad and step off carefully.
Shake out your hands. Let your breathing slow down.
That's your walk for today. Well done.
All done. Every minute counts, and you did them all.
That's it for today. Your journey just moved a little further.
Let's head out. Start with an easy stroll.
Out the door we go. Nice and easy for the first couple of minutes.
Keep one ear free so you can hear what's around you.
Pick up the pace a little. Keep an eye out for curbs.
Quicker steps, but watch the ground ahead.
If it's warm, look for shade, and take a sip of water.
A little quicker now. Swing your arms and walk tall.
Ease back to a comfortable stroll.
Find somewhere to sit or lean, in the shade if you can.
Let's walk home gently. Easy pace from here.
Slow down to an easy stroll to finish.
Lovely walk. When you're home, your chair moves are waiting, if you'd like them.
One.
Two.
Three.
Four.
Five.
Six.
Seven.
Eight.
Nine.
Ten.
Eleven.
Twelve.
Three, two, one.
Ten more seconds.
Five more seconds.
Thirty seconds left.
One minute left.
Halfway there.
Last one.
Two more.
Rest for twenty seconds. Sip some water if you like.
Now the other side.
You're doing it.
Nice and steady. That's exactly right.
Your pace is the right pace.
Small steps still add up.
Look at you, keeping it going.
That's a little stronger than last time.
Take it easy on yourself. You showed up.
Lovely. Keep breathing.
You're almost there.
Every minute here counts.
Take your time. Sit down, sip some water, and breathe slowly.
Whenever you're ready. There's no hurry.
Welcome back. Let's ease back in, nice and slow.
That's a good place to stop. Today still counts.
Let's take care of that.
Here's an easier version. Go gently.
We'll skip that one. On to the next.
Let's stop here. Rest up, and we'll adjust your plan.
Stand behind your chair. Hold on if you need to.
Hold the chair the whole time. Only let go if you feel steady.
Paused. Take all the time you need.
If you feel dizzy or unwell, stop and sit down.
You've reached Central Park Zoo. Your journey through New York starts here.
You've made it to Bethesda Fountain, right in the heart of the park.
Welcome to Times Square. Bright lights, and you walked here.
Bryant Park. A green, quiet corner in the middle of the city.
You've arrived at Union Square. Just a little further to the bridge.
You made it to the Brooklyn Bridge. That's the whole of New York. Well done.
Welcome to Cades Cove, a quiet valley in the Smoky Mountains.
You're in Sarria, where the last stretch of the Camino begins.
Portland Head Light, standing tall on the coast of Maine.
Carmel-by-the-Sea. Your walk along the Pacific coast begins.
Nice walking. Now a few chair moves.
Let's finish with a gentle stretch.
Next up.
Chair moves today. Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat.
That's all your moves for today. Nicely done.
Your joints are a bit achy today, so we'll keep it gentle.
A steady one today.
Feeling good today? Let's make the most of it, at your pace.
Welcome back. Your journey is right where you left it.
Good to have you back. Let's start with an easy five minutes.
We made today a little shorter. Build up at your pace.
You're ready for a little more. Today we'll try the next level.
We'll keep things seated for now. That's a smart choice.
A little extra today. Just a few minutes.
Time for a gentle stretch. Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat on the floor.
We'll move slowly and breathe. Stretch to a gentle pull, never to pain.
Stand behind your chair and hold the back with both hands. Feet about hip-width apart.
Lovely walking. Stay seated, and let's cool down with a few easy stretches.
Ease into it slowly.
Go only as far as feels comfortable.
Breathe in through your nose… and out through your mouth.
Breathe into it. Let your shoulders stay soft.
A gentle pull is enough. No bouncing.
Keep breathing. There's no need to push.
If it pinches or hurts, ease off a little.
Let's start on the left.
And the other side.
Come back to the middle… and now the other side.
Once more, just as gently.
And slowly come back.
Gently release, and sit tall.
Relax. Notice how that feels.
Next one coming up.
Here's an easier way. Smaller and slower is just as good.
That's your stretch for today. Take one more slow breath.
Nice and easy. You gave your body some care today.
All done. Sit for a moment, and have a sip of water.
Neck turns. They make it easier to look over your shoulder.
Sit tall, shoulders down, and look straight ahead.
Slowly turn your head toward your shoulder, as far as is comfortable.
Just turn halfway, nice and slow, and keep your eyes open.
Now the side of your neck.
Rest your right hand on your left shoulder, and let that shoulder stay low.
Slowly tilt your head to the right, ear toward your shoulder. No pulling.
Skip the hand, and just tilt your head a little.
Chest and shoulders. Good for sitting tall.
Sit forward, away from the back of your chair.
Draw your shoulders back and down, open your arms to the sides, and lift your chest gently.
Rest your hands on your hips, and just draw your shoulders back.
Upper back twist. It helps with turning to reach for things.
Cross your arms and rest your hands on your shoulders. Feet flat.
Turn your upper body to one side. Your hips stay still, your head turns with you.
Turn just a small way. That's plenty.
Side stretch.
Sit tall with your feet flat and a little apart.
Reach one arm up and over your head, and lean gently to the other side.
Keep your arm by your side, and just lean a little.
The back of your thigh. It makes bending down a little easier.
Sit near the front of your chair. Stretch one leg out, heel on the floor, toes pointing up.
Rest your hands on your other leg, and lean forward from your hips, keeping your back long.
Keep that knee a little bent, and lean forward only a little.
Ankles. For steadier steps.
Hold the side of your seat, and lift one foot just off the floor.
Point your toes away from you… then bring them back toward you. Slow and smooth.
Keep your heel on the floor, and just lift and lower your toes.
Calf stretch. Hold on to your chair the whole time.
Hands on the back of your chair. Step one foot back, and keep both feet flat.
Bend your front knee a little, keep the back leg straight and the heel down. You'll feel it in your calf.
Take a shorter step back, and let your back knee bend a little.
